CNBC, 27 Oct 2026

Stock futures were little changed early Tuesday following a winning session on Wall Street, with traders looking ahead to a slew of corporate earnings and the start of a Federal Reserve two-day policy meeting.

S&P 500 futures were down 0.1%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were up 0.11%. Nasdaq-100 futures are down 0.25%.

In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 1.73% higher, while the Topix rose 0.61%. South Korea's Kospi gained 3.09%, while the small-cap Kosdaq rose 2.29%. Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.46%. Mainland China's CSI 300 closed 1.32% lower.

Wall Street kicked off the week on a solid note. The Dow climbed 146.42 points, or 0.3%. The S&P 500 gained 0.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.8% as tech shares outperformed. The artificial intelligence trade got a boost after Anthropic filed to go public at the Nasdaq. This would mark another major tech IPO for 2026, following SpaceX's blockbuster listing in June.

Tesla shares advanced more than 5%, while Nvidia climbed 2%. Microsoft and Amazon also rose on the day.

Those gains come as the artificial intelligence trade has faced pressure from investors worried companies in the space are borrowing too much cash to fund their AI build-outs.

On Tuesday, traders will pore through a deluge of third-quarter earnings reports. Coca-Cola, Robinhood and Boeing are among the companies set to post results. Tech giants Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are due out later in the week.

The Fed is also set to kick off its latest monetary policy meeting. While the central bank is expected to keep rates unchanged, traders will look for clues on whether another rate hike will take place before year-end.

"If, as expected, there is no change in rates, it will still be interesting to see what the vote is after the swings in the last two meetings," wrote Thomas Block, Washington policy strategist at Fundstrat. "While the Fed views itself above partisan politics, it would be unlikely that the Fed would move rates a week before a national election."

On the economic front, traders will be watching for durable orders, consumer confidence data and the new home sales report.

HSBC's London-listed shares dropped 6.5% in early European deals Monday, putting them on course for the worst session since Apr. 3 2025, after the lender reported a slight miss on consensus expectations for pre-tax profit and revenue in the third quarter.

Europe's largest bank also announced a share buyback of up to $1 billion.

Citi analysts called it a "mixed set of results," noting a 2% miss on revenue expectations but an 18.8% return on tangible equity in the year to date, significantly ahead of its medium-term guidance of around 17%.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 was down 0.27% shortly after 8:07 a.m. in London (4:07 a.m. E.T.) as the continent's major bourses and regional sector opened the session in mostly negative territory.

Basic resources led gains, rising 0.68%, followed by media stocks, which added 0.25%, and healthcare names, which advanced 0.38%.

Banks led losses, tumbling 1.18% in early dealmaking, with utilities down 0.39% and household goods shedding 0.21%.

The U.K. FTSE 100's was 0.93% lower in London, while in Paris, France's CAC 40 was 0.28% lower. In Frankfurt, Germany's DAX slipped 0.17%, and the Italian FTSE MIB was down by 0.29% in Milan.

Novartis hiked its profit outlook early Tuesday, as the Swiss drugmaker said it achieved sales growth despite a challenging backdrop of generic competition.

It now expects core operating income for 2026 to grow in line with the low single digits, up from previous expectations of a small decline.

It comes as the company posted third-quarter sales largely in line with FactSet expectations of $14.5 billion, up 4% year-on-year.

Novartis took a $1.9 billion hit from a partial impairment of its del-desiran drug for muscle-wasting disorder in the quarter, resulting in reported operating income declining by 61% in constant currencies. On an adjusted basis, operating income grew 10%, beating analysts' expectations.

The results follow a trio of clinical setbacks Novartis posted last month, sending shares to their worst day in six years and raising investor questions about its acquisition strategy. It included the failure of del-desiran in a late-stage trial, an asset Novartis bought through its $12 billion acquisition of Avidity Biosciences earlier this year.

"You have to stay courageous and really push to really find breakthroughs if you're going to grow a company of our size," CEO Vas Narasimhan told CNBC Tuesday.

Luxury German carmaker Porsche said Tuesday that its profit rose in the first nine months of the year after undergoing restructuring, amid struggles in the Chinese market.

The Volkswagen-owned company said operating profit rose to 1.74 billion euros ($1.94 billion) in the first nine months, a jump from 40 million euros the previous year. Meanwhile, sales revenue was down 5.9% to 25.28 billion euros, while deliveries declined 16% to 178, 532.

Porsche said the market environment in China "remains challenging," as it battles with weaker demand in the region in recent years due to increased localized competition.

The company announced plans to reduce its total workforce by 25% by 2035, while reducing management by 40% as part of its cash-saving strategy.

"Even in a challenging market environment, Porsche is showing itself to be financially robust," Dr Jochen Breckner, a member of the executive board for finance and IT, said in the report.  "We achieved a solid operating result in the first nine months while simultaneously generating strong net cash flow.

"This, combined with our robust balance sheet, gives us the strength we need to consistently continue on our chosen path."

Brent crude futures for December delivery — the global price benchmark — were trading just above the flatline shortly after 3:05 a.m. E.T., at $115.84 per barrel.

West Texas Intermediate futures for December delivery, a snapshot of U.S. oil prices, dropped almost 0.1% to $101.65 a barrel.

The choppy direction in oil prices follows talks between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan and Iranian officials on Monday, aimed at keeping diplomatic channels open, as U.S. President Donald Trump continues to mull a step-up in military operations against Tehran as the conflict enters its ninth month.

Stock markets in Europe are set to start Tuesday session in the red, with Stoxx 50 futures seen 0.32% lower ahead of the market open.

France's CAC 40 was 0.28% lower,  with Germany's DAX set to start the day down 0.35%, and the Italian FTSE MIB off by 0.37%.

Meanwhile, U.K. FTSE 100 futures were 0.51% lower.

Europe's largest bank HSBC on Tuesday reported third-quarter pretax profit that largely met analysts' estimates complied by the lender, and announced a share buyback of up to $1 billion by the end of this year.

Revenue at HSBC rose to $18.6 billion from $17.8 billion in the same period last year, while banking net interest income rose 6%, alongside the bank clocking higher fee income form its corporate and institutional banking and wealth business.

The bank approved a third interim divided of 10 cents per share.

The earnings come as HSBC is reportedly considering significant job cuts in its U.K. wealth management business, as part of a broader push to adopt artificial intelligence.

China's industrial profits last month grew at their strongest pace since June, as a boom in manufacturing tied to artificial intelligence offset drag from persistently weak domestic demand.

Profits at large industrial firms rose 14.4% in September from a year earlier, official data released Tuesday showed. For the first nine months of this year, industrial profits climbed 15.5%, slightly below the 15.7% rise in the January-September period.

The strength comes as industrial earnings swung to double-digit growth earlier this year, following a modest gain in 2025 and three straight years of declines, helped by Beijing's efforts to curb rampant price wars across sectors and surging demand for AI-related equipment.

The Korea Exchange activated a buy-side sidecar on the Kospi, temporarily halting program trading, as South Korean stocks surged.

A buy-side sidecar is triggered when the Kospi 200 futures index rises 5% or more for at least one minute, stopping trading for 5 minutes.
